notes.title: Dev Diary #4
notes.notes: [p]Hello everyone!  [/p][p]Roads of Rage is going to release on June 30th 2025 at about 11am PDT! It's price will be $8 with a 10% launch discount. We have chosen to release the game without a publisher or major marketing strategy with the hope that granting players full access to our game will show the hard work and features we put into Roads of Rage over it's year long development. [/p][p][/p][p][b]Change of plans?[/b][/p][p]Whereas before we wished to hold off release for the sake of adding features and building awareness, we've had a change of heart after learning about Steam's "grey zone", which describes games who sell well on Steam that nobody knows about. Additionally, there's talk among seasoned indie dev veterans how the secret to indie game success is that there is no secret, such that sheer chaos and randomness grant success to little known indie devs like us. If that is indeed true, then our old plan to withhold release to gather wishlists, marketing, and a publisher has only hindered our overall success. No more idling by, it's time to put Roads of Rage out there.[/p][p][/p][p][b]A look back[/b][/p][p]Like all good ideas, Roads of Rage emerged from a long car drive and a shower, the moments when our mind opens to the inspiration particles flowing within cosmic background radiation. It began with an acknowledgement of no new beat 'em ups, which turned into a non-human beat 'em up game, which turned into a car beat 'em up. "Roads of Rage", a pun and a reference to one of the oldest beat 'em ups, after that the game practically wrote itself. A large country with little public transportation has fostered a culture of vehicles, we need only look around to see the archetypes and personalities of car characters. Month after month of relentless coding, debugging, and working with freelancers eventually built our game. We then took a step further by adding many more features like minigames, color customization, and accessibility like total input customization. We pushed the idea of Roads of Rage to it's naturally end and then some with what little resources at our disposal, and that alone makes us proud. "You never work on a masterpiece, you always work towards it."[/p][p][/p][p][b]Can you help us?[/b][/p][p]We are unpublished, which means we need your help more than ever. There is a growing resentment towards AAA games and their corporate strategies. In fact, big name publishers are the #1 scapegoat for canceled, incomplete, and overpriced video games. If you, cherished reader, seek to change the gaming industry into a utopia of low prices and developer support, then help us spread Roads of Rage to the public (specifically to Reddit, which has a strict no self-promoting rule). Roads of Rage is designed to fill a niche in the gaming industry by being the only car beat 'em up, but it will not be our only game. Harness Games plans to continue making unique and fun games, the quality of which will only improve with your support. Additionally, a successful Roads of Rage will grow with future patches of additional levels and content. Help us spread creativity throughout the industry and propagate video games as the greatest artform of our time![/p][p][/p][p]As always, thank you for supporting indie devs like us![/p][p]-Harness Games[/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary #3
notes.notes:
Hello everyone! 
A free demo for Roads of Rage is now available to download on itch.io and steam! We're hoping that giving players access to gameplay will provide a deeper insight into our game. After all, gameplay is the unique feature of gaming as an artform that no other art can provide, to become part of the artwork itself.

Demo only contains the tutorial and level 1, but should also include all other game features like local co-op, controller support, accessibility options, car customization, etc. Level 1 should provide a good summary of our gameplay loop; fight cars using cartial arts and special moves, progress the level, build your combo counter and use fun items, encounter the end of level boss, and finally finish with our Outrun inspired minigame.

If you encounter any bugs, please let us know by DMing us on X, @harnessgames. Development has been an interesting journey that has lasted about a year now. We believe video games are the greatest artform of our time, and with that comes the added con of being the hardest art medium to create. For startups like us to take on such a Hyperion task begs the question, why work so hard for something with no guarantee of success/no one cares about? That is what we believe to be the meaning of ambition. It is our source of motivation beyond fame or fortune leading us to do the impossible when the impossible doesn't want to be done. That is the power we harness from games and will continue to harness, 
if necessary, for years, if necessary, alone.

As always, wishlist Roads of Rage, share with others, and thanks for supporting indie devs like us!

-Harness Games

notes.title: Dev Diary #2
notes.notes:
Hello everyone! 
Version 0.9.0 is now live, this is a large update because we added player character customization! 

[b]Colorful[/b]! Players now have the option when selecting their favorite car to change the car's color to any RGBA value they desire. We are particularly proud of this, as we previously thought the task to be Sisyphean. However, in exploring Gamemaker's shaders and devising sprite covers, we were able to circumnavigate around the requirement of making multiple, multiple sprites to change colors for each animation, for each cutscene, for each character, and so on. Instead, we constructed a universal solution in the game's code, saving tons of time and resources! But again, this is something that only a game dev is really proud of, players will probably just look at this function and think "huh, neat!"

[b]Combat changes[/b]! We've also revamped the combat, giving players the option to swap out special moves to 2 of the available 5 instead of having all 5 outright and relying on player exploration to discover them all. It is possible for anyone to go back to the old combat, simply hit esc 5 times on the title screen and type in Allspecials to revert to old combat. However, we believe the new combat is better, based on playtester feedback noting a lack of customization and too many available moves. Removing all special availability lets players focus more on combat with succinct inputs, all while maintaining player agency to choose which special moves they like the most.

[b]Guns! Guns! Guns![/b] A gamer once told me, put a gun in your game and I'll play it. I hope others share this sentiment, because we've added guns, 3 in fact! As part of the new combat, players now have a weapon attack, which can be a Machine Gun, a Missile Launcher, or a Grapple Hook. Guns add an extra juicy feature to combat, giving the player multiple options to engage even when at a distance. It's really satisfying to spam the machine gun, or snipe a distant enemy with a missile, or pull in an enemy with the grapple hook to begin a combo. Just about everyone I met during development who wanted to give unsolicited ideas has mentioned, you should put in guns or missiles! Mission accomplished!

As always, wishlist Roads of Rage, share with others, and thanks for supporting indie devs like us!

-Harness Games

notes.title: Dev Diary
notes.notes:
Hello everyone! 
Development for Roads of Rage is trucking along. Atm we're in search of a publisher to help with game marketing and sales, localizations, and QA testing. We also have a twitter account, @harnessgames if you'd like to reach out to us with any questions or opportunities. In the meantime, we're hard at work fixing bugs and adding bits. Please wishlist Roads of Rage and encourage others to do the same, wishlists help gather the attention of publishers and are an easy way for anyone to support us! 

We're also getting a MacOS build together, but Apple isn't making it easy. Not only do they require you to own a Mac, but it must be a relatively new version in order to run the latest Xcode. Not to mention the extra $100 needed to pay for 1 year of development, which itself wasn't seamless (seamful?) and required several calls to Apple support, who were in fact very helpful, no fault there.

We're happy with the newly designed visuals for our minigames, which add a more Outrun aesthetic as we want the player to feel like they're driving to the next location or exploring Road City. Next, we'll be looking into ways to improve in-game visuals and possibly make tweaks to combat, maybe redesign special moves to be combo finishers. Naturally, every bug we find is terminated.

As always, thank you for supporting indie developers like us!

-Harness Games
